title: Michigan fires Jason Beck: Wolverines will owe significant buyout after parting with struggling OC in Year 1 - CBS Sports
description: A dismal 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State proved to be the breaking point for a unit ranking near the bottom of
body:
A dismal 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State proved to be the breaking point for a unit ranking near the bottom of the FBS in scoring and total offense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, the school announced on Sunday, one day after a 15-6 loss to Michigan State in which the Wolverines managed only 192 total offensive yards. Offensive line coach Jim Harding will serve as interim offensive coordinator for the remainder of the season.Beck, the nation's highest-paid offensive coordinator, came with head coach Kyle Whittingham after a successful year together at Utah last season. That success never translated in Ann Arbor, however, on a 5-4 Michigan team that is one of the most disappointing in the country. The loss to Michigan State was the final straw. "The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense," Whittingham said Sunday. "We need to put our offensive players and the entire team in the best possible position to be successful."We appreciate the hard work and effort that Jason has dedicated to the program. Jason is a great man and coach, and unfortunately, it did not work out the way that we wanted it to at Michigan. We wish Jason and his family nothing but the best in the future."Michigan already made a quarterback change earlier in the season, benching highly paid former five-star quarterback Bryce Underwood in favor of freshman Tommy Carr. The offense never really got going, however, and ranked 125th in passing offense, 126th in scoring offense and 132nd in total offense out of 138 FBS teams.
Beck's firing comes with a significant financial hit for Michigan. The Wolverines will owe Beck as much as $10.2 million to buy out a three-year deal that paid him $2.8 million this season and was set to go up to more than $3 million the next two seasons, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. It could be the most expensive assistant coach buyout ever, though it is subject to offset mitigation. The pressure had been building on Whittingham to make a move as the offense continued to flounder this season. The noise got particularly loud after a 13-6 loss to Indiana in which the Wolverines managed only 57 rushing yards on 42 carries. Michigan had one of the nation's most expensive rosters, sources told CBS Sports, and had especially invested big on the offensive side of the ball. Beck was never able to fit the pieces he acquired into the system he wanted to run, however. It will be interesting to see whether it provides a spark to an offense that is in desperate need of one. As CBS Sports first reported last month, Whittingham's job security could also be in question. Michigan is in the middle of an AD search to replace outgoing AD Warde Manuel and would like to find its next athletic department leader before deciding on Whittingham, according to sources. But it is not out of the realm of possibilities that Whittingham could be one-and-done in Ann Arbor, especially if he continues to lose games.
"I think they know this isn't the long term," one industry source told CBS Sports. "It's just, do you rip it up after one year?"

schema.headline: Michigan fires Jason Beck: Wolverines will owe significant buyout after parting with struggling OC in Year 1 - CBS Sports

title: Army vs. Navy 2026 uniforms: Black Knights unveil tribute to 'Ivy Soldiers' for annual rivalry game - CBS Sports
description: Army will honor the division's legacy with intricately detailed threads as they look to
body:
Army will honor the division's legacy with intricately detailed threads as they look to snap a two-game skid against Navy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Army Football
            
            

    
        Army will sport an "organic camouflage" look for its Dec. 12 rivalry showdown with Navy, as the Black Knights don special uniforms that will pay tribute to the 4th Infantry Division. Known as the "Ivy Soldiers," the division boasts a legacy dating back to World War I.The threads will specifically pay homage to 4th Infantry Division soldiers from the 2014-19 Operation Atlantic Resolve. As the Black Knights seek to snap a two-game losing streak against the Midshipmen, they'll do so in threads loaded with symbolism. "In the 25 years since the attacks on September 11th, Ivy Soldiers have been at the forefront in answering the nation's call," said narrator Michael Strahan on Army's announcement of the uniforms. "We will strive to emulate their dominance of any type of battlefield and consistent capability to always be ready and forward when we take the field against our rivals."Details go all the way down to the cleats, which incorporate 3D-embossed ivy vines weaving into the edges of Nike's swoosh. Above the numbers on the jersey backs — where player names would be emblazoned for most teams — each of Army's uniforms will simply read "Ivy soldier."
A total of 25 Ivy Soldiers have earned the Medal of Honor during the Division's 100+ year history. The early line in this year's game, which will be played at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, favors Navy by 2.5.

schema.headline: Army vs. Navy 2026 uniforms: Black Knights unveil tribute to 'Ivy Soldiers' for annual rivalry game - CBS Sports

title: Former Ohio State players sound off on program, Ryan Day after humiliating loss to Oregon: 'Clean house' - CBS Sports
description: The Ducks scored 38 straight points against the Buckeyes, prompting several program legends to share their opinio
body:
The Ducks scored 38 straight points against the Buckeyes, prompting several program legends to share their opinion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Several former Ohio State players sounded off on the Buckeyes' catastrophic performance during Saturday's 41-28 home loss to Oregon, a setback that all but detonated the program's College Football Playoff hopes this season.Ryan Day's fifth loss in his last 11 games dating back to last season put a negative spotlight on a program with one of college football's most talented rosters, just two years removed from a national championship under his guidance.Former Ohio State defensive lineman Tommy Schutt, who hadn't tweeted in six years before Saturday night, noted it was time to "CLEAN HOUSE" after an "embarrassing" performance at home. Curtis Samuel, a former All-Big Ten wideout for the Buckeyes, made his first appearance on "X" in three years with a series of comments in the wake of the loss."Can't allow a team to come in the shoe and be the bully that's unacceptable and for sure not the culture," Samuel wrote, mentioning  five-star freshman Legend Bey and his lack of usage in another message.
Ex-Ohio State standout Beanie Wells, who rushed for 3,382 yards and 30 touchdowns over three seasons in the mid-2000s, went long-winded on the program and the Buckeyes' soft play defensively."The eye in the sky doesn't lie and this doesn't just start last week against USC," Wells said on CBS Sports HQ. "You go back to the game vs. Indiana, the explosive plays and inability to get to the passer on a consistent basis. Those things have always been there with his defense and now everybody's starting to take notice. This is something Ohio State went out and put on film weeks ago and nobody took notice because they got away with the victory at Indiana."These holes and these issues have been there, Now they're being exposed when they're losing on a national scale when you're supposed to be separating yourself."
The Buckeyes have lost consecutive games for the first time since 2011 and Day's third loss in a single season is the first time that's happened for him since he took over eight years ago."Ohio State is revealing who they've always been and those issues are showing themselves and this is why the committee is viewing themselves they way they did," Wells said. "They were at home against a wounded Oregon team and you did nothing, you did not respond. You were up 14-0 and you showed me all you can be a frontrunner, you can't get punched in the mouth and respond like Oregon did."Oregon scored 38 straight points after trailing by two touchdowns early before Ohio State fans started leaving Ohio Stadium early in the fourth quarter. Ranked No. 12 in last week's first CFP Top 25, the Buckeyes will likely tumble down the poll in Tuesday night's update (they came in at No. 20 in Sunday's coaches poll). 
"We didn't expect any of this to happen," Day said. "I thought the way that we came out was how we thought we would play in this game. And then once the momentum swung, we weren't able to stop that and then swing it,"

schema.headline: Former Ohio State players sound off on program, Ryan Day after humiliating loss to Oregon: 'Clean house' - CBS Sports

title: Richmond's Jack McCaffery, son of Penn coach Fran McCaffery, on leave after Hodgkin's Lymphoma diagnosis - CBS Sports
description: McCaffrey, the son of Penn coach Fran McCaffrey, transferred from Butler to Richmond this offseason
body:
McCaffrey, the son of Penn coach Fran McCaffrey, transferred from Butler to Richmond this offseason
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
Richmond forward Jack McCaffery, the son of Penn coach Fran McCaffery, will be on indefinite medical leave from the team after being diagnosed with Hodgkin's Lymphoma, the school said in a statement on Sunday. McCaffery spent his freshman season at Butler and transferred to Richmond this past offseason."We are grateful to the Richmond coaching staff and medical team for their prompt response, and to Kevin Mahoney and the doctors and nurses here at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania," McCaffery said in a statement. "He is in great hands and our family feels blessed to be here, where Jack's care is directed by this world-class care team."At Butler last season, McCaffery appeared in nine games and averaged 2.8 points and 1.6 rebounds before his season ended due to an illness and complications from having his wisdom teeth removed. McCaffery's older brother, Connor McCaffery, was an assistant coach on Butler's staff during his time with the team."From the moment Jack arrived at Richmond, he's been an important part of our program," Richmond coach Chris Mooney said in a statement. "He's a tremendous teammate who has earned the respect of everyone around him through his hard work, character and commitment to doing things the right way, both on the court and in the classroom. Our entire program will be there for him and his family every step of the way on his path to recovery." McCaffery was a four-star recruit in the 2025 recruiting cycle by 247Sports and the No. 144 overall player in the class.

schema.headline: Richmond's Jack McCaffery, son of Penn coach Fran McCaffery, on leave after Hodgkin's Lymphoma diagnosis - CBS Sports

title: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR to undergo MRI after suffering knee injury on final snap, per report - CBS Sports
description: The Rams do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the wide receiver will undergo i
body:
The Rams do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the wide receiver will undergo imaging on Monday to confirm
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Los Angeles Rams are holding their breath over the status of star wideout Puka Nacua. The All-Pro pass catcher is set to undergo an MRI on his knee after injuring it late in the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders, according to a report from ESPN. The team reportedly does not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging set to be done on Monday will determine the severity of the injury. Nacua suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of the game for Los Angeles with 1:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. He took a third-and-11 handoff from Matthew Stafford for a 5-yard gain. Nacua got up after a hard hit, but the injury will now be further evaluated. 
This injury dampens what was otherwise a stellar day for the wideout. He finished with 14 receptions on 19 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, while adding 20 yards rushing. Nacua was the key to the Rams' success in the 20-13 victory that helped bring Los Angeles back over .500 on the season. 
Nacua is slated to miss time, which further dents what is already a banged-up receiver room. The Rams have already placed fellow wideout Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring he suffered in Week 6 against the Cardinals. That injury is expected to sideline him for anywhere from six to 10 weeks when he suffered it. This isn't the first injury Nacua has sustained this season, previously missing time this season with a hip injury. When he's been on the field, however, he's been among the best wideouts in the NFL and has caught a touchdown in four of his last five games played. 
If he's going to miss any time with this latest injury, it could embolden the Rams to make a move for a receiver prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.

schema.headline: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR to undergo MRI after suffering knee injury on final snap, per report - CBS Sports

title: Chiefs looking to trade for wide receiver, GM Brett Veach tells NFL on CBS' Tracy Wolfson - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City has one of the NFL's least-productive wide receiver corps in 2026
body:
Kansas City has one of the NFL's least-productive wide receiver corps in 2026
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Chiefs GM Brett Veach told NFL on CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson that Kansas City is looking to add a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, though "some of the major franchise players they've looked at are off the market," Wolfson reported during the Chiefs' Week 9 game against the Jets.
Wolfson specifically mentioned the lack of deep passing, something that's been a major issue ever since Tyquan Thornton suffered a significant injury in Week 4. Patrick Mahomes did not complete a single 20+ yard pass from Weeks 5-8 (three games), tying the longest streak of his career.Currently, the Chiefs are leaning on Xavier Worthy and Rashee Rice as their top wide receivers. Worthy entered Week 9 having recorded 25 or more receiving yards just twice this season, and Rice is more of a quick-game, yards-after-catch weapon. Other wide receivers on the roster are fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen, 2025 fourth-round pick Jalen Royals, undrafted second-year player Andrew Armstrong and return specialist Nikko Remigio.Through eight weeks, only the Raiders' and Vikings' wide receivers had fewer receiving yards.There are several wide receivers thought to be available ahead of Tuesday's deadline, though, according to Wolfson's report, some of the biggest names floated might not be on the table. Veach and Co. will keep pushing before the clock strikes 4 pm. ET on Tuesday, marking the end of the trade period.
The Chiefs (5-2) had lost two straight entering Sunday.

schema.headline: Chiefs looking to trade for wide receiver, GM Brett Veach tells NFL on CBS' Tracy Wolfson - CBS Sports

title: Browns' Shedeur Sanders claims 'smiling' comment about Saints defense was taken out of context - CBS Sports
description: However, Sanders claims he doesn't care about how the Saints' defense feels
body:
However, Sanders claims he doesn't care about how the Saints' defense feels
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is trying to put out the fire he claims he wasn't trying to start. Sanders says he didn't intend to give the New Orleans Saints bulletin board material ahead of their Week 9 matchup, even though his comments came across that way to his opponents. "Everything I do up to this point is taken out of context, but I can't be one caring about what people say," Sanders told CBS Sports' AJ Ross pregame. "I would never disrespect or ever talk down another opponent or another team, so that's just another trick in the media that they use. However they feel, they feel. I don't care how they feel."  Sanders will make his first start of the season on Sunday with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol. As such, he conducted a media availability session ahead of the contest on Wednesday and made an eyebrow-raising comment about the Saints and a defense that ranks 28th in yards per game allowed and 29th in scoring."I've seen a lot," Sanders said with a grin when asked what he noticed on film. "When I smile, just know that means something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing. I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile whenever it's just, like, some questions, you know?"Sanders may not have criticized the New Orleans defense outright, but his body language made it clear that he saw a unit he could pick apart during his film study. The second-year player would be far from the first quarterback to have his way against this squad, which allows 233.3 yards per game through the air, but the Saints might come out with additional motivation to stop him in the wake of those remarks.
Count edge rusher Carl Granderson among those who saw what Sanders had to say."We're gonna come in with a chip on our shoulder for sure," Granderson said. "They've been chirping a little bit. We see what the quarterback done said. We're finna come in hot and ready to play. We're going to pack the defense, and the offense is going to come with it. It's going to be a good game for sure. We're going to come out with the dub."Dating back to his college career, Sanders has long been a lightning rod for attention off the field. The former fifth-round pick and son of Deion Sanders is never one to avoid speaking his mind.
For the first time this season, Sanders gets the opportunity on Sunday to back up his talk with his play on the field. He briefly entered last week's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers when Watson took a big hit in the first quarter, but he attempted only two passes and has thrown just three times this year. The Week 9 start will mark a return to the starting lineup for the first time since last season, when he spent seven weeks as the Browns' No. 1 quarterback.

schema.headline: Browns' Shedeur Sanders claims 'smiling' comment about Saints defense was taken out of context - CBS Sports

title: Sorting through the College Football Playoff picture after Week 10 produced more carnage - CBS Sports
description: Week 10's slate of games added yet another emphatic chapter to what has been a chaos-filled 2026 season
body:
Week 10's slate of games added yet another emphatic chapter to what has been a chaos-filled 2026 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first weekend of November delivered carnage. Next comes the response from the College Football Playoff selection committee.At-large résumés were put to the test Saturday, leaving several contenders without breathing room entering the final weeks. Survive and advance sounds simple enough until one team's best-case scenario requires other teams to lose.How many squads can actually exhale entering Week 11?I am separating the playoff picture into three groups: teams we consider locks, programs in good position and the all-important bubble, where every remaining possession carries postseason consequences. That last sampling will include coaches politicking for the selection committee's ear as early as this week.The selection committee gave us three hard takeaways from their first set of rankings: quality wins matter, when those games happened is significant and the new conference strength metric is paramount. 
Battle for first-round byeTeams in this tier: Georgia (8-1), Utah (9-0), Indiana (8-1), Miami (8-1), UCLA (9-0), Notre Dame (8-1), Alabama (6-2)These seven teams are in the best shape for a first-round bye should they win out. Six are in the mix to earn a Power Four conference champion designation, which may get them bonus points over Notre Dame. Georgia's victory at Ole Miss, coupled with Alabama's blowout of LSU, puts the Bulldogs and Crimson Tide on a collision course to meet in Atlanta, provided both teams win their remaining games.After holding off BYU in Salt Lake City, Utah is the favorite to win the Big 12. The Utes will play Texas Tech for a league title should both win out from here. The Red Raiders go to Oklahoma State in Week 11, while Utah tries to stay unblemished at Arizona -- the Utes' toughest remaining game.
How far will No. 1 Miami fall? That depends on the selection committee's interpretation of how much this team changes moving forward without Malachi Toney. Losing close at Notre Dame, though detrimental, should not diminish opinions surrounding the Hurricanes. They play Duke, who could enter the rankings this week, before finishing with Virginia Tech and Boston College.In the Big Ten, Indiana and UCLA have the most direct paths to a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. The Hoosiers host USC next weekend while UCLA, No. 8 in the first CFP reveal, entertains Illinois on Friday night. USC's on the bubble, but can strengthen its at-large case over the next three games. More on that in a bit.Lastly, Notre Dame is safe as a CFP entry following its 31-24 win over Miami. The CFP selection committee surprised most of us after slotting the Fighting Irish at No. 11 in their first rankings, but they've potentially halved the distance from outside the top-10 to creeping up on the top 4 now after one of the season's top victories of year despite the Hurricanes playing without one of their top players. With an expected 11-1 finish, Notre Dame is guaranteed a first-round home game if not one of the top-4 seeds with some chaos down the stretch elsewhere.
These are the seven teams who most closely appear like locks to make the 12-team bracket. That term is used with hesitancy given the rash of parity we've seen this season and the likelihood of more upsets coming over the rest of the month.At-large hopefulsTeams in this tier: Texas (7-2), Tennessee (7-2), Boise State (8-1)Beyond the top-four seeds, which we expect will be given to the champions of the SEC, Big Ten, Big 12 (if Utah), and ACC (if Miami), as noted, there are three teams that have built impressive resumes entering Week 11.Texas has more ranked wins (4) than any other team and is unbeaten this season in ranked matchups. Ranked No. 7 as the fourth-best SEC team in the first selection committee reveal behind Georgia, Alabama and Kentucky, we're expecting the Longhorns to at least move to No. 6 on Tuesday night, if not higher. They have the best chance in the country to get in with just nine wins. 
Behind the Longhorns in the at-large discussion, Tennessee's blowout win over Kentucky was a second signature victory for the Vols at home this season. Tennessee, despite beating Alabama by 16 points on Oct. 16, was not viewed in the same "pod" as the Crimson Tide last week, according to CFP selection committee chair Hunter Yurachek. We're anticipating that Saturday night's drubbing of the No. 6 Wildcats should narrow that margin between the Vols and Alabama in a few days.Unbeaten in the Pac-12 with its only loss this season coming at Oregon in the opener, Boise State is the frontrunner for the Group of Six's highest-ranked team bid. Ironically, the CFP selection committee didn't reveal too much of their hand last week by putting the Broncos at No. 24 -- meaning we have no idea how close others in the Group of Six picture (New Mexico, perhaps) are to Boise State. The Broncos had no issues dispatching Colorado State without quarterback Maddux Madsen on Saturday night and now enter next weekend's home game with Oregon State essentially looking at a must-win unless they want the streaking Lobos to surface in the conversation.Bid thievesTeams in this tier: Texas Tech (8-1), Wake Forest (8-1), BYU (7-2), Kentucky (7-2), USC (7-2)
If you're keeping score, that's 10 teams we've given you in the bracket with two at-large spots remaining. From here, you look at potential bid-stealers that could "win" their way into the bracket. We're starting with one-loss Texas Tech and Wake Forest, teams that were ranked 15th and 16th heading into Week 10, as destiny-controllers in the Big 12 and ACC.Should the Red Raiders and Demon Deacons win out, they'll lock in playoff appearances as conference champions. That would mean Texas Tech has a win over Utah in December, while Wake Forest's lone impressive victory would've come against Miami in Charlotte that same weekend. Looking at the respective resumes and metrics, it does not appear that either team has a path to an at-large berth with another loss -- which could include both finishing 11-2 overall after losing in conference championships.After Saturday's loss at Utah, BYU needs major help. The Cougars must win out and hope for chaos down the Big 12's final stretch, which must include another setback for Texas Tech, and tiebreaker wins over Houston and others just to get to the league title game. That said, BYU's win over Notre Dame holds after the Fighting Irish's victory over Miami. At 10-2 overall on Selection Sunday, BYU would be squarely on the bubble. Right now, the Cougars are projected as our "last team in" in that specific scenario if other conference championship races go chalk.
Kentucky squandered its shot at winning out and playing for a conference title, but still should be an at-large selection as long as the Wildcats hit that magic number of wins from the SEC. We're putting that at 10, meaning Kentucky must beat Florida, Missouri and Louisville the rest of the month to be scribbled into the first round. That's plausible for first-year coach Will Stein, but far from a certainty.The most important number in this grouping is two -- the number of losses USC has right now. If the Trojans beat Indiana next weekend, handle Maryland and then take out unbeaten UCLA during rivalry weekend, Lincoln Riley will have his first CFP appearance at the program. That would mean USC finished red-hot with four consecutive Big Ten victories and would clinch a spot in the conference championship game to boot.On the bubbleTeams in this tier: Ole Miss (6-3), Ohio State (6-3), LSU (6-3), Oregon (6-3), South Carolina (6-3)
This is where the conversation gets really interesting. Oregon just blew out Ohio State, Ole Miss lost by 35 points at home, and LSU dropped a much-needed game against Alabama. Furthermore, South Carolina is streaking with four straight wins and now has a potential injury to quarterback LaNorris Sellers to worry about -- and for the selection committee to grade.Ohio State's playoff hopes are diminishing with consecutive losses. Don't take Buckeyes entirely off the board, but it's close. The last thing anyone expected was a humiliating home defeat in Week 10 against the Ducks, and Ohio State should be outside of the top 15 on Tuesday night. Lane Kiffin has zero ranked wins in his first season at LSU. The selection committee placing the Tigers at No. 14 last week is all you need to know about their belief in this team. LSU does host Texas in Week 11 and goes to Tennessee in Week 12. Win both of those and finish 9-3 overall and the conversation changes a bit with a pair of resume-building victories.
South Carolina is one of the wild-cards here. The Gamecocks travel to Arkansas next week, then host potentially top-ranked Georgia on Nov. 21. No team in the country has a bigger chance to alert the selection committee in the final stages than the Gamecocks if they topple the Bulldogs. South Carolina won six straight games in 2024, finishing 9-3, but was left out of the bracket. This time around, winning out would mark seven consecutive victories, including a couple over likely playoff entries.

schema.headline: Sorting through the College Football Playoff picture after Week 10 produced more carnage - CBS Sports

title: Bill Belichick makes surprise return to Patriots ahead of New England's Week 9 showdown vs. Packers - CBS Sports
description: Belichick has kept his distance since leaving New England after parting ways in 2023.
body:
Belichick has kept his distance since leaving New England after parting ways in 2023.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Bill Belichick smiled when asked about Rob Gronkowski's induction into the New England Patriots Hall of Fame following North Carolina's win over Connecticut on Saturday. Later in the day, Belichick surprised many by taking part in a dinner celebrating one of the many accomplishments he and the Patriots had during his 24 seasons as the team's head coach. Following his team's 38-21 win over UConn on Saturday, Belichick drove to Foxborough to take part in a dinner celebrating the 10-year anniversary of the Patriots' Super Bowl LI win, their 34-28 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons and the fifth of six Super Bowl wins under Belichick. The Patriots' celebration of that team coincided with Gronkowski's Hall of Fame induction. Along with Belichick, Tom Brady also attended the festivities. Brady was in attendance for Gronkowski's formal induction into the team's Hall of Fame on Saturday. Belichick recently attended a dinner celebrating the 40th anniversary of the New York Giants' first Super Bowl win. Belichick was the Giants' defensive coordinator during the franchise's first two Super Bowl wins. Belichick was noticeably absent when the Patriots recently celebrated the 25th anniversary of the franchise's first Super Bowl championship team. 
It's worth noting that Patriots owner Robert Kraft was not present at Saturday night's dinner, which was held at Davio's Steakhouse at Patriots Place. Kraft, 85, is currently recovering from back surgery. Belichick and Kraft don't appear to be on the best of terms, and Belichick has kept his distance from the franchise since he and the Patriots parted ways after the 2023 season. The two have exchanged barbs in the media in the years since their breakup. Last September, Belichick confirmed reports that Patriots scouts were prohibited from being at North Carolina's facilities. "It's clear I'm not welcome there at their facility. So they're not welcome at ours," Belichick said at the time. 
Kraft did say last year that he plans to build a statue for Belichick, whose time as Patriots coach included six Super Bowl wins, nine AFC titles and 17 AFC East division crowns.

schema.headline: Bill Belichick makes surprise return to Patriots ahead of New England's Week 9 showdown vs. Packers - CBS Sports

title: Kirk Cousins trade rumors: Raiders have received no calls, reportedly want to keep QB - CBS Sports
description: Despite speculation connecting Cousins to a reunion with the Vikings, the Raiders repor
body:
Despite speculation connecting Cousins to a reunion with the Vikings, the Raiders reportedly are not interested in moving their starting quarterback
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Imagn Images
            
            

    
        Week 9 is underway across the NFL, but looming over all the on-field action is what's happening behind the scenes ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. One of the most intriguing names floating around the rumor mill is Kirk Cousins. The Raiders quarterback has been looked at as an expendable piece for Las Vegas, especially with Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft, waiting in the wings. However, it doesn't sound like Cousins is going to wear a new uniform once Week 10 rolls around. The Raiders have not received any trade calls this weekend regarding Cousins, according to ESPN. Moreover, Las Vegas is reportedly not interested in dealing him either. They want to stay the course with their plan to keep Cousins as their starter until they believe Mendoza is ready. 
Taking a methodical approach to Mendoza's development has been first-year coach Klint Kubiak's stated approach since the offseason. So far, they've held to that as Cousins has started every game for the organization this season. Entering Week 9, Cousins has 19 passing touchdowns, which is second in the NFL and only looking up to Joe Burrow in Cincinnati (20). He's also completing 63.6% of his passes with a 101.4 passer rating over his first eight starts. The Raiders enter Week 9 at 4-4 on the season and still within striking range of a wild card spot, which is likely why Las Vegas is apprehensive about moving Cousins. 
While the team is currently holding firm, it will be interesting to see if that changes, particularly after Week 9. One team that has been linked to Cousins has been the Minnesota Vikings, whom he played for from 2018 to 2023. With Kyler Murray dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring injury, they do have a need at quarterback as they make a playoff push, entering Week 9 with a 6-1 record and in first place in the NFC North.

title: College football odds, lines, schedule for Week 11: LSU, Indiana open as favorites in key conference battles - CBS Sports
description: Indiana hosts USC in a pivotal Big Ten clash while Georgia, LSU and unbeaten Utah navigate tricky conference test
body:
Indiana hosts USC in a pivotal Big Ten clash while Georgia, LSU and unbeaten Utah navigate tricky conference tests as the playoff race heats up
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 11 of the college football season doesn't carry the same curb appeal as Week 10 in terms of ranked vs. ranked matchups. But it is nonetheless littered with challenging games for College Football Playoff hopefuls and national championship contenders. At a time when parity is more prevalent than ever, landmines are everywhere.It's not as if this coming Saturday is void of high-end games. Indiana hosts USC on CBS in a Big Ten showdown brimming with intrigue for both. The Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) have been playing with fire all season but have only been burned once (so far). Now they welcome a 7-2 USC team that slayed Ohio State before a Week 10 bye.With another marquee win, USC's odds of reaching the CFP will surge while Indiana's case for inclusion will become undeniably shakier. The Hoosiers' marquee win at this point is either Northwestern or Nebraska, and mediocre foes Washington and Purdue are all that remain for IU after USC.Week 11 lines are out, so let's take a look at what oddsmakers are thinking as we look ahead. 
Odds via SportsLine consensusThe big gamesMissouri at Georgia (-14): Georgia is the last SEC team left with fewer than two losses in league play. The Bulldogs are in the driver's seat to reach the SEC Championship Game and are the clear national title favorites (+240 at FanDuel) after dismantling Ole Miss 42-7 in Week 10. But it should be noted that a AP top-2 team has lost in five consecutive weeks. Missouri is limping in after getting some bad breaks in a 34-20 loss to Texas. However, the Tigers looked like an even match for the Longhorns and have been great in spurts this season.Texas at LSU (-4): Are we sure that LSU is 100% completely cooked when it comes to the College Football Playoff? There could be a glimmer of hope if the three-loss Tigers can pull off back-to-back wins over Texas and Tennessee (on the road) before ending the season at lowly Arkansas. LSU still rates well in predictive metrics, and it has two big-time resume-enhancement opportunities over the next two weeks.USC at Indiana (-7.5): Five of Indiana's six Big Ten games have been decided by one possession. Will this be the sixth? USC is riding high off a Week 9 home win over Ohio State and now must prove it can beat an elite team on the road after cross-country travel. A win here would drastically alter the outlook for Trojans coach Lincoln Riley positively and leave Indiana's CFP resume in tatters. Betting against Cignetti at home after a bye seems unwise.
Utah (-2.5) at Arizona: This spot is ripe for chaos. With Utah coming off an emotional rivalry win and one of just two unbeaten teams left in the FBS ranks, it must travel to take on a capable Arizona team. The Wildcats got an extra day of rest following a Friday night win over TCU in Week 10 and will be yearning to prove they belong among the Big 12's elite after dropping games against BYU and Texas Tech earlier this season.Illinois at UCLA (-8.5): UCLA is aiming to reach 10-0 under first-year coach Bob Chesney. To do it, the Bruins will have to get through a surging Illinois team that has won four straight Big Ten contests following a 2-3 start. It's been a remarkable turnaround for coach Bret Bielema's club, which already has 11-point wins over Oregon and Nebraska under its wing.Duke at Miami (-14.5): One week after the emotional letdown of a big comeback that ended with defeat at Notre Dame, Miami needs to be on its best behavior against Duke. The Blue Devils have outscored their last two ACC foes 88-5 as running back Nate Sheppard continues to tear the league apart. The 'Canes passing defense is typically more vulnerable than its run defense, but they can't get caught snoozing after a high-intensity trip to play the Fighting Irish.

title: Giants' J.J. McCarthy returns against Eagles after hip injury sent QB to locker room - CBS Sports
description: Jameis Winston briefly entered the Week 9 contest in relief of McCarthy
body:
Jameis Winston briefly entered the Week 9 contest in relief of McCarthy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The New York Giants appear to have survived another injury scare at the quarterback position. J.J. McCarthy returned to Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles after spending time in the sideline medical tent and locker room while being evaluated for a hip injury.With McCarthy initially deemed questionable to return, the Giants turned back to Jameis Winston, who started four games before McCarthy replaced him atop the depth chart. Winston led a touchdown drive before he headed back to the sideline.McCarthy took a hard hit to his lower abdomen on a quarterback keeper in the third quarter. Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop McCarthy's run and made contact with McCarthy's side on the tackle.
McCarthy attempted to throw on the sideline before heading to the locker room and was in obvious pain after he completed his throwing motion. He grabbed at his side and fell to the turf as medical staff came to his assistance. Despite the clear discomfort, he was able to get back into game action just before the end of the quarter.
The Giants were mostly quiet on offense during McCarthy's Week 9 start and scored only six points before he left with the injury. McCarthy was 9-for-13 for 101 passing yards and ran three times for another 11 yards ahead of his brief exit.Although it seems that McCarthy will remain in action beyond this week, if the injury acts up on him and forces him to miss time, his potential absence may be a significant blow to the NFC East-leading Giants. Already without Jaxson Dart for the rest of the year due to the torn knee ligaments he suffered in Week 2, New York traded for McCarthy as a potential season-long solution. His effectiveness upon insertion into the lineup in the fourth quarter of the Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints and in his first start the following week came as a pleasant surprise and gave the Giants reason to believe they could maintain their division lead.
Winston has been serviceable in his own right, so perhaps the Giants could stay afloat if they are ever forced to hand the keys back to him. He went 2-1-1 in his four starts before McCarthy replaced him, and that stretch included a 326-yard performance in the tie with the Washington Commanders and a 250-yard outburst the previous week in a victorious effort. Winston's lack of consistency has long been a limiting factor in his ability to command an offense as a starter, however.

title: 10 NFL trades that need to happen: Derrick Henry to Patriots, Budda Baker to Bills among options - CBS Sports
description: Kirk Cousins returns to Minnesota, George Pickens heads to Las Vegas and more aggressive moves contenders should
body:
Kirk Cousins returns to Minnesota, George Pickens heads to Las Vegas and more aggressive moves contenders should make before Tuesday's trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:41 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline is just two days away, and it's already been a dramatic time around the league. The Seattle Seahawks beefed up their offensive line with Quenton Nelson, the San Francisco 49ers brought back DeForest Buckner, the Chicago Bears look like a Super Bowl favorite with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, and the Baltimore Ravens have a new quarterback in Jacoby Brissett. Who is the next domino to fall?A total of 27 players were traded in-season last year. That's the most in the past 25 years. A total of 12 players were dealt on deadline day last year. Get ready for a wild 48 hours. There's a lot of speculation around Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but will he actually get dealt? What about the Minnesota Vikings? Could they swing a deal for a new quarterback in the next 48 hours? Below, we will break down 10 trades that need to happen.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Kirk Cousins to the VikingsVikings receive: QB Kirk CousinsRaiders receive: Conditional fifth-round pickESPN's Adam Schefter got a lot of people excited last week when he said he was going to keep an eye on the Vikings. Are they going to trade for Justin Herbert? Or Mac Jones? Maybe Daniel Jones? What about bringing back Kirk Cousins?It doesn't appear that Cousins will be dealt at the trade deadline, but it would be a storybook ending if Kevin O'Connell brought Cousins back to town and he contributed to a Super Bowl run. Cousins spent six seasons in Minnesota, threw for 4,000 yards four times and went 50-37-1 as the starter. While he's 38 now, Cousins is still capable of playing good football. His 19 passing touchdowns entering Sunday ranked second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow, and his 265.5 passing yards per game ranked seventh. 
Now that we are halfway through the 2026 season, the Raiders can turn their attention to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, while Cousins will improve a Vikings passing attack that's sputtering. Kyler Murray's 170.3 passing yards per game entering Week 9 ranked 30th among 31 qualifying passers, and we don't know if Carson Wentz is a solution. Justin Jefferson is sick of not having consistent play under center, so let's get Cousins back to Minnesota and watch him power a Super Bowl run.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Budda Baker to the BillsBills receive: S Budda BakerCardinals receive: Third-round pickHow long can the Bills keep winning track meets? Josh Allen can outscore just about any team, but this defense ranks bottom 10 in both yards allowed per game (352.1) and points allowed per game (25.9). Buffalo has four wins in games the defense has allowed 30 points!Adding Cardinals safety Budda Baker should help. He's an eight-time Pro Bowler playing great football for a not-so-great team. In eight games this season, he's recorded 51 tackles, four passes defensed, one interception and a career-high 3.5 sacks. Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30 — just Bobby Wagner, Roquan Smith, Luke Kuechly, Lavonte David, Ray Lewis, Fred Warner and Budda Baker. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Derrick Henry reunites with Mike VrabelPatriots receive: RB Derrick HenryRavens receive: Third-round pickMike Vrabel has a few former Titans on his roster, including A.J. Brown and Kevin Byard. He could swing a deal for another one of his former players in Derrick Henry.The Ravens running back is averaging 76.6 rushing yards per game and has scored nine total touchdowns in nine games played. Given the injuries at the quarterback position and the fact that the Ravens are the only team in the division with a losing record, it looks like Baltimore won't be making its Super Bowl run this year. Henry is 32 going on 33 and should be helping a contender.The Patriots rank 12th in rushing yards per game with 123.1, but Rhamondre Stevenson is averaging under four yards per attempt and about 46 yards per game. TreVeyon Henderson's situation remains unclear as well, after he revealed he experienced an "unusual medical emergency." Vrabel knows what Henry is capable of as a bell cow, and he can help the reigning AFC champs get back to the "Big Game."

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. George Pickens off to 'Sin City'Raiders receive: WR George PickensCowboys receive: Second-round pickGeorge Pickens ranked third in the NFL in receiving yards last season with 1,429 and nine touchdowns on 93 receptions, but this season has been a different story. His yards per game has dipped from 84.1 to 66.6, and Pickens played just 56.8% of snaps during the Cowboys' Week 8 loss to Arizona. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag this year and is due a massive contract. Questions remain about the Cowboys' ability to pay him. Dak Prescott is the No. 2 highest-paid quarterback in the NFL, CeeDee Lamb is the No. 6 highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL and Tyler Smith is the No. 2 highest-paid guard in the league. Then, the recently added Joey Porter Jr. is due a massive contract as well. Is Dallas really going to pay Pickens around $35 million per year? It makes sense to pick up a second-round pick for a player who may not be on your roster next year. The Raiders, on the other hand, have one of the worst wide receiver rooms in the NFL.Tre Tucker leads the way with 474 yards, then Jalen Nailor is behind him with 113 yards. Pickens would provide Fernando Mendoza with a true perimeter threat for years to come. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Broncos add Breece HallBroncos receive: RB Breece HallJets receive: Third-round pickBreece Hall signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal this offseason after being slapped with the franchise tag. He became the Jets' first 1,000-yard rusher since 2015 and is one of three active players to record 3,000 rushing yards and 1,500 receiving yards in his first four seasons. However, Hall's quad injury opened the door for Braelon Allen, who has really taken advantage of his opportunity. He rushed for a career-high 147 yards against the Raiders last week. The Broncos' rushing offense entered Sunday ranked seventh-worst in the NFL. While rookie Jonah Coleman has flashed in spots and the injured RJ Harvey is a weapon as a receiver out of the backfield, Hall would immediately upgrade an inconsistent offense that has legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Josh Downs to Kansas CityChiefs receive: WR Josh DownsColts receive: Conditional fourth-round pickThe Chiefs would like Brian Thomas Jr., but they don't want to give up a second-round pick for a player with some question marks. They instead trade a conditional fourth-round pick for Josh Downs, who has recorded the second-most receiving yards out of the slot ever since he was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of North Carolina. 
Downs caught 30 passes for 330 yards and one touchdown in his first eight games this season and put up a career-high 803 yards and five trips to the end zone in 2024. The Chiefs' issues at wide receiver are well-documented. Rashee Rice entered Sunday averaging 48.6 receiving yards per game, and Xavier Worthy is just a gadget player at this point. Travis Kelce shouldn't be leading this team in receiving. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Ladd McConkey to the SteelersSteelers receive: WR Ladd McConkey, fifth-round pickChargers receive: WR Roman Wilson, second-round pickCBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo pitched this trade earlier this week, and it makes some sense. Ladd McConkey could take the Steelers' passing attack to another level, while former Michigan head coach Jim Harbaugh would reunite with Roman Wilson. 
McConkey has caught just 17 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown through the first eight weeks of the season. As a rookie, he caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns. The Steelers have averaged 26.2 points per game over their last six, but their leading receiver, DK Metcalf, is averaging just 47.3 yards per game. In McConkey, Aaron Rodgers would get a solid slot weapon who could also act as a security blanket.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Tony Pollard to the GiantsGiants receive: RB Tony PollardTitans receive: Fourth-round pickJonathan Taylor has gotten a lot of oxygen over the past few weeks, but there's another running back in the AFC South that teams should be interested in. Tony Pollard rushed for 129 yards and three touchdowns against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 and then 117 yards and two touchdowns against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. He's averaging a career-high 74.4 rushing yards per game this season, and he ranks top 10 in rushing attempts, rushing yards and rushing touchdowns. He and Derrick Henry are the only players to have rushed for 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons.The Giants do have Cam Skattebo, who rushed for 124 yards and a touchdown in that overtime win against the Houston Texans, but Pollard would upgrade a questionable room as New York looks to win the division. John Harbaugh was upset his team couldn't land Jeffery Simmons. Mike Borgonzi finally answers the phone and sends Pollard to the Giants.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Moro Ojomo to the JagsJaguars receive: DT Moro OjomoEagles receive: Third-round pickThe Jaguars have reportedly been sniffing around for defensive linemen, and Moro Ojomo could be a fit. Jacksonville just saw DaVon Hamilton go down with a torn quad, and GM James Gladstone hopes to make an addition to maintain one of the best run defenses in the NFL. Ojomo adds some juice as a pass rusher from the interior and has recorded the second-most pressures on the Eagles over the last three seasons behind Jalen Carter. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Khalil Mack moves north to Santa Clara49ers receive: EDGE Khalil Mack, sixth-round pickChargers receive: Third-round pickReports indicate that Khalil Mack won't be traded, but this is a player who should be rushing the passer for a contender. The former Defensive Player of the Year turns 36 in a few months, but he can still get after the quarterback. Mack recorded three sacks in his first seven games this season and notched a career-high 17 sacks just three years ago. 
The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (142) entering Sunday. The defensive line has 47 games missed by players, the most in the NFL. Mack would help a Raheem Morris defense that can win a Super Bowl if healthy.

title: Mario Cristobal 'beyond upset' at ACC officiating after Miami's loss at Notre Dame - CBS Sports
description: The Hurricanes coach was livid over an apparent Elija Lofton touchdown reception that was ruled incomplete
body:
The Hurricanes coach was livid over an apparent Elija Lofton touchdown reception that was ruled incomplete
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Miami coach Mario Cristobal says he's "beyond upset" with the explanation for the ruling that negated Elija Lofton's potential game-tying touchdown reception in the fourth quarter of the No. 1 Hurricanes' 31-24 loss at No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday night.Miami's tight end appeared to make a catch near the boundary of the end zone on fourth-and-6 from the Notre Dame 18 late in the game, but the play was ruled incomplete after Fighting Irish safety Luke Talich dislodged the ball from Lofton's grasp as he stepped out of bounds. The original call on the field stood as incomplete following a brief replay review."Really, really disappointed that they negated Elija Lofton's touchdown with two hands on the ball and two feet in bounds, but like we told our team before we left Miami, do not leave it in the hands of the officials because that's what you're going to get out here," Cristobal said in his postgame news conference. "I'm pissed off. It's bullshit, and I'll leave it at that. That's the way it was seen by them. So I got to live with it and respect it, and our players got to live with it, and we got to do better. Again, don't leave it in the hands of the officials."
Miami quarterback Darian Mensah sprinted toward Lofton after he thought it was a successful touchdown reception with 3:36 to play. Mensah finished 24-of-43 for 276 yards and three touchdowns, including one to Lofton and a pair to Cooper Barkate, who led all pass-catchers with 10 receptions for 92 yards.
"I didn't even see him knock the ball out at the end, so I thought it was a touchdown," Mensah said. "You can't leave it up to one play. Can't leave it in the hands of the officials. I've got to play better."Cristobal later apologized for criticizing officials."I need to be mature and professional about it," he said. "Be very honest about my opinion on it, but not point any fingers except at ourselves and go get better." Playing without the injured Malachi Toney for the first time this season, Miami's offense didn't catch fire until the third quarter when the Hurricanes trailed 24-3. Behind a Heisman-caliber performance from CJ Carr, Notre Dame finally notched its signature win and moved closer to the College Football Playoff as a result.
"It's a special moment," Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said after avenging last season's 27-24 loss to the Hurricanes that ultimately kept the Fighting Irish out of the CFP. "Enjoy the moment, because tomorrow when you wake up it's time to get ready for the next one. I know it's a big one. This is big. This is special. I'm not going to sit here and say this was like the other ones. No, this is different."

title: Tomorrow's Top 25 Today: UCLA surges into the top 10, Virginia dominates Arkansas for big statement win - CBS Sports
description: What will college basketball's AP Top 25 look like on Monday? Here are our predictions after a week featuring a f
body:
What will college basketball's AP Top 25 look like on Monday? Here are our predictions after a week featuring a few consequential ranked-on-ranked matchups
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first week of the 2026-27 college basketball regular season has come and gone. When the next AP Top 25 poll is released on Monday, the top four will remain the same. Florida, Duke, Illinois and UConn all went 2-0 this week, which included the No. 1 Gators picking up a statement win over in-state foe No. 14 Miami and the No. 4 Huskies defeating No. 16 Michigan in a rematch of last season's national title game.Hours after Florida picked up an opening-night win over Miami, one of the first big upsets occurred in Las Vegas when UCLA defeated former Pac-12 rival Arizona. The Bruins were ranked No. 22 in the preseason poll and should receive a healthy boost in the rankings after beating a top-five team. Meanwhile, Arizona shouldn't be punished much in the rankings for a quality loss and should remain somewhere in the top 10.Days later, UConn made a statement in Boston with a win over Michigan behind a huge performance from its starting backcourt of Silas Demary Jr. and Braylon Mullins. UConn will remain at No. 4 in the poll this week, but it's clear to see why Dan Hurley's squad should be considered a Tier 1 title contender this season after that performance.
        
            
                Rare opening-week title game rematch doubles as a familiar warning: UConn is yet again a national title threat
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The other big-time matchup on the slate this week saw No. 9 Virginia defeat No. 12 Arkansas on Sunday. The Cavaliers should move up a few spots in the polls on Monday after the impressive win.
Here is how we project the rest of the poll to look on Monday. The lone team projected to drop out of the poll: Iowa State.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. FloridaFlorida showed why it deserved to open the season No. 1 after recording a statement win over Miami. The Gators have the best frontcourt in college basketball. The next test? A matchup on the road against another in-state foe: Florida State. Last week: 1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. DukeDuke's margin of victory combined in its wins over Army and Coastal Carolina: 95. The schedule does get significantly tougher with a matchup against Michigan State in the Champions Classic on Tuesday. A week after that, Duke faces Illinois. Last week: 2

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. IllinoisIllinois put up 120 points in a season-opening win over Fairleigh Dickinson and followed it up with a 112-point outburst against Penn. The Fighting Illini project as one of the top offenses in college basketball once again. The scary part? All-American forward David Mirković hasn't even played yet. Last week: 3
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. UConnUConn took care of business and made a statement with a win over reigning national champion Michigan in Boston. The Huskies have one of the best backcourts in the country and showed why they're a Tier 1 title contender this season. Last week: 4
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Michigan StateJeremy Fears Jr. began his national player of the year campaign by posting 13 points and 11 assists in a blowout win over Quinnipiac. He followed it up by nearly recording another double-double (12 points, nine assists) in a win over Toledo. Sparty will be tested against a deep Duke roster next week in Chicago. Last week: 6

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. TexasTexas improved to 2-0 with a blowout win over Chicago State. The Longhorns won't be tested until they have an interesting showdown against Baylor next weekend. For now, all is good with Sean Miller's squad. Last week: 7
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. VirginiaVirginia made a statement on Sunday with a 91-72 win over No. 12 Arkansas, with four different players finishing in double figures. The Cavaliers will get a slight boost in the polls on Monday. Last week: 9
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. UCLAUCLA should receive a huge jump in the rankings after defeating No. 5 Arizona 84-75, followed by a blowout win over North Florida. In the win over North Florida, star freshman Nikola Kusturica had his coming-out party by recording 29 points, six rebounds, three assists, and two blocks. He is only 17 years old but plays well beyond his years. Last week: 22

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. ArizonaDespite losing its opener to UCLA, we project Arizona to remain in the top 10. The Wildcats bounced back after their loss to UCLA by defeating Cal Poly for their first win of the season. Motiejus Krivas dominated in the win over Cal Poly and scored 30 points. Last week: 5
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. TennesseeIt's hard to draw any definite conclusions about Tennessee after beating Wofford 90-59. While it's possible the Vols just stay at No. 8, I'm projecting that UCLA jumps them in the poll and Arizona slides right in front. Tennessee won't be tested until it faces Michigan State on Nov. 17. Last week: 8
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. HoustonHouston opened the season with a convincing win over La Salle and is in action on Sunday night against Cal. Last week: 10

                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. LouisvilleLouisville is 2-0 after picking up a 50-point win over Morehead State. Five-star freshman Obinna Ekezie Jr. was impressive in that game and finished with 20 points and 12 rebounds. Last week: 11
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. GonzagaGonzaga opened the season with an impressive win over Purdue and followed it up with a 41-point win over New Mexico State. The Bulldogs likely will remain at No. 15 on Monday. Last week: 15
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. ArkansasAfter losing to Virginia on Sunday, Arkansas is projected to drop a few spots. However, the Razorbacks won't be punished for losing to a top 10 team. Last week: 12

                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. St. John'sSt. John's took care of business against Iona on Sunday, moving to 2-0. That game was a homecoming of sorts for Rick Pitino, who coached Iona before taking the St. John's job in 2023. Last week: 13
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. KansasTrey Kaufman-Renn got his first start in a Kansas uniform against Middle Tennessee and finished with 17 points in 18 minutes. The Jayhawks have a huge showdown upcoming against Kentucky in the Champions Classic. Last week: 17
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. Texas TechTexas Tech improved to 2-0 with wins over Jackson State and Bethune. The real test will come against No. 3 Illinois at home on Tuesday. If the Red Raiders win that game, they will almost certainly jump into the top 10. Last week: 19

                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. MiamiMiami should take away lessons from its loss to No. 1 Florida on opening night. The Hurricanes are still a very good team that will be dangerous in ACC play. A loss to the top-ranked team in the country should see Miami drop only a handful of spots. Last week: 14
                            
    
                                                
                    
    19. AlabamaAlabama scored 197 points during its first two games of the season against Sam Houston and Arkansas State, which should come as no surprise because Nate Oats-led teams always have an elite offense. Star wing Amari Allen posted the fifth triple-double (16/13/11) in Alabama basketball history during its win over Arkansas State. Last week: 20
                            
    
                                                
                    
    20. MichiganMichigan couldn't buy a bucket when it needed one against UConn. The Wolverines shot poorly from the 3-point line in each of its first two games. That was one of the Wolverines' strengths last season. Still, a loss to No. 4 UConn shouldn't keep Michigan out of the rankings this week. Last week: 16

                            
    
                                                
                    
    21. USCUSC opened the season with a blowout win over Milwaukee and is in action late Sunday night against Wichita State. Last week: 21
                            
    
                                                
                    
    22. KentuckyKentucky got a scare on Friday when James Madison proceeded to knock down 15 3-pointers during the Wildcats' 89-80 win. All is good for now for Mark Pope's team, but a matchup against Kansas looms. Last week: 23
                            
    
                                                
                    
    23. VanderbiltVanderbilt improved to 2-0 after recording a 23-point win over Wake Forest at home. Star guard Tyler Tanner recorded a double-double with 17 points and 10 rebounds.
